data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH COMPLETE — not truncated. The research phase logged a completion block at 06:32 ET and amended it at 06:37 after a late finding, so nothing here was cut off mid-sentence. 16 candidate lines resolved to 13 distinct symbols; all 13 are published and none were dropped on the reward-to-risk floor.

WHY THE SHAPE IS WHAT IT IS. Four of the thirteen are exits or risk reduction (TLT and LCII close outright; DHT, DINO and XLE are stop raises on open positions) and two more say explicitly to wait (LULU and AVGO, both reporting within 30 hours). That is the honest shape of a day with 23 open positions, several of which carry no stop at all, into a regime that inverted inside two weeks. Position updates do not add new risk.

ZERO INTRADAY IDEAS, stated plainly rather than padded. Every equity price in this report is the 2026-09-01 close, roughly 14 hours old at synthesis with the market not yet open, and there was no 08:30 ET print today. There was no honest basis for a level-precise same-session trade, so none was manufactured. Eleven swing, two long_term. No conviction-5 ideas either: nothing today had multiple independent confirmations AND a clean counter-argument, because the dominant driver is a war.

CONCENTRATION IS THE MAIN RISK IN THIS REPORT, more than any single idea. The thirteen ideas are four bets, each at or under the three-name correlation cap. Driver A, Strait of Hormuz transit closure: DHT, DINO, XLE — treat as ONE bet of roughly 6.5% of capital, not three of 2%. Driver B, destroyed Qatari liquefaction: EQT, CRK, CEG — this one does NOT end with a ceasefire, since the trains need three to five years regardless. Driver C, the rate and inflation consequence: TLT exit, IYR short, KXFEDDECISION October hike. Driver D, idiosyncratic: CCJ, LULU, AVGO, LCII. The second-order truth: A, B and C all trace to the same war. A ceasefire helps C while hurting A, so the book is partially self-hedged, but a sustained escalation wins on every line at once. That is the definition of concentration and it should govern sizing. Note also that the LCII exit leans on the same rate move as Driver C; it is classified as idiosyncratic because it reduces exposure rather than adding it.

THE LATE FINDING THAT CHANGED THREE IDEAS. At 06:33 ET research found that the labour market is already contracting — payrolls fell 23,000 in July against a +80,000 forecast, with June revised down to +20,000. That cuts directly against Driver C, which needs the Fed to keep hiking. All three Driver C ideas were re-captured at lower conviction as a result: TLT from 4 to 3, IYR from 3 to 2, and the October hike contract from 3 to 2 with its price cap lowered from 31c to 29c. IYR additionally carries an explicit stand-down gate on Friday's print. This is why the two conviction-2 ideas exist and why they are sized as lottery tickets.

SIZING ADJUSTMENT MADE IN SYNTHESIS. IYR was captured at 1.5% and is published at 1.0%, the conviction-2 cap in config/strategy.md. No other candidate exceeded its cap.

REWARD-TO-RISK CLUSTERING — checked, and it is not target-fitting. Every ratio here was recomputed in code from the final entry, target and downside rather than trusted from the notes. Three land close to the 2.0 swing floor: TLT 2.06, LCII 2.05 and EQT 2.12. Each level was derived before the ratio was computed — TLT's 78.30 from roughly 17 duration against a 10y at 5.05%, LCII's 89.00 is the actual 150-day low, EQT's 63.00 is chart resistance between the close and the 180-day high of 68.24. XLE shows 4.37 only because its new-money entry sits close to the raised stop; if XLE never trades back to 63.00 the new-money leg simply does not happen and the update is purely the stop consolidation to 61.40.

FAILED SOURCES AND PRICE GAPS. Yahoo returned HTTP 429 for all index, futures and volatility symbols, so there is NO VIX level, NO DXY level, and no live crude print in this report — 'crude above $95' is sourced from news reporting, not from a fetched quote, and is labelled as such in market_context.levels. All equity and ETF prices are finnhub quotes at the 2026-09-01 close (session: pre-market, age ~872 minutes at synthesis); they were re-quoted during synthesis and were unchanged, because the market has not opened. Event-contract prices are live Kalshi bid/ask at 06:20 ET. Research could not enumerate a Kalshi series for the jobs report, and Robinhood's prediction-markets economics page lists only Fed decisions, so there is no event-contract expression of Friday's payroll print despite it being the most important date in this report. Gasoline event markets were found but Robinhood availability could not be verified, so they were not traded.

COVERAGE GAP: NO NEW SMALL CAPS. CRK at roughly $4.7bn is the smallest new name. Research recorded the reason rather than an excuse: every small cap reachable in the time available sat inside a driver already at its correlation cap (FRO under A, FLNG and the LNG shippers under B), and opening a fourth driver properly needed more time than remained. A micro cap researched in ten minutes is a guess, not a lottery ticket. Carried forward for tomorrow.

POSITION DECISIONS THAT DO NOT FIT THE IDEA SCHEMA are in the watchlist and must not be skipped: close all four BTC and /MBTU6 shorts (stops breached by 15-19%); TJX and BCC are stopped out and should not be re-entered; attach stops to NKE at 36.20 and PFE at 26.80, both of which have been carried with no stop at all; cancel the stale resting orders in VST (134.00, 128.00), DG (119.00, 121.00) and BCC (76.50).

TRACK RECORD CONTEXT. The book is 0 for 9 on closed trades at an average of -3.3%. That sample is under the ~15 needed to mean much, but it is not encouraging, and it is part of why today's report leans toward attaching stops and taking profits rather than adding new risk.

=== RED TEAM (phase 2c, 06:40-06:55 ET) ===

CORRECTION TO THE CONCENTRATION PARAGRAPH ABOVE, which is the most important
line in this report and is wrong as written. It says "a ceasefire helps C while
hurting A, so the book is partially self-hedged." It is the other way round.
Driver C is three ways of being short duration: exiting TLT removes a long-end
long, the IYR short needs yields higher, and the October hike contract needs the
inflation impulse to persist. A ceasefire collapses crude, takes the inflation
impulse out, pulls yields down and loses on all three — which is precisely what
each of those ideas says in its own key_risk field ("A US-Iran ceasefire
collapses crude and takes it to single digits"; "a ceasefire unwinds crude, the
inflation impulse and the hike odds together, and IYR opens through the 106.40
stop"). The book is not partially self-hedged. Escalation wins on every line and
a ceasefire headline loses on essentially every line at once, including both
exits, which would have sold near the low of the news cycle. Only LULU, AVGO and
the LCII exit sit on the other side, and they are the three smallest claims here.
Post-red-team the escalation-correlated capital is roughly 12% (XLE 2.5, DINO 2,
DHT 2, CCJ 3, EQT 2.5, CEG 1, IYR 1, KXFEDDECISION 1, less the CRK cut). Size it
as one position, because on a ceasefire morning it will behave as one.

WHAT WAS CUT. CRK, from rank 5. Its only differentiator over EQT — Haynesville
basis capture into Gulf Coast liquefaction — is negated by its own
counter-argument, which concedes the scarcity rent accrues to terminal owners
until new trains commission. Its published entry condition said to own EQT
instead if it does not pull back, which is the author conceding it is not a
second idea. Full reasoning is on the watchlist entry.

WHAT WAS DOWNGRADED. Both conviction-4s, on the principle that a 4 that is wrong
gets sized larger than a 3 that is wrong. CCJ 4 to 3: the new leg of its thesis —
that the war made energy security concrete — was tested on the tape on
2026-09-01 and failed, with CCJ -2.53%, URA -3.45% and UEC -5.31% on the day
crude cleared $95 and XLE printed an all-time high; what is left is the crowded
three-year consensus story the idea's own counter-argument concedes. EQT 4 to 3:
on timeframe, not direction — the rebuttal to its counter-argument is explicitly
a multi-year contracting mechanism, which cannot underwrite a swing target 6.06
ATR away in 15 sessions. CEG 3 to 2 and 2.5% to 1.0%: its own counter-argument
says the fuel-cost mechanism reaches revenue with a multi-year lag "if at all"
and that the stock is actually priced on datacenter contracting news, so the
market is pricing a different variable than the thesis; the only direct evidence
is one session of relative strength inside a complex down 22-50%. There are now
no conviction-4 ideas in this report.

WHAT WAS FIXED RATHER THAN CUT. XLE: the 4.37 reward-to-risk is the largest
number in the report and is entry geometry, not edge — the new-money entry sits
1.60 above the raised stop, and the 70.00 target has no resistance behind it
because the fund is at an all-time high. Flagged in the idea; the actionable
content is the stop consolidation to 61.40. DINO: the 108 to 116 target raise is
what took computed reward-to-risk from 1.55 (below the floor) to 3.00, which is
the exact failure mode this phase exists to catch. The target survives only
because it has a peer-relative anchor the original text omitted (DINO +11.8%
against PBF +139% and CVI +118% over 150 days), and the disclosure is now written
into the idea so the reader can discount it. IYR: the counter-argument claimed a
1.5% size against a published 1.0%; corrected, and the inconsistency with the TLT
idea is now stated — TLT is an exit rather than a short because the growth case
for the long end was judged too strong to bet against, yet IYR is that same bet
with equity beta on top. AVGO: the "margin mix, not demand" entry gate is softer
than it reads, because that distinction will not be cleanly resolvable live on
the call; the honest default is no trade.

RE-RANKED, and on a modified rule that is worth stating. Conviction first as
usual, but within the conviction-3 block the tiebreak is evidence quality and
time-criticality rather than raw reward-to-risk, because two of the largest
ratios here (XLE 4.37, DINO 3.00) are the ones this review just flagged as
geometry artifacts, and ranking on them would put the weakest numbers on top.
The two exits lead because they must be done at the open, followed by the three
stop raises, then new risk. That ordering also matches the report's own framing
of today as a risk-reduction day against an 0-for-9 closed-trade record.

TWO VALIDATOR ARTIFACTS THE ENFORCE PASS WILL ACT ON, recorded here so the
demotions are not misread as substantive.

(1) The Kalshi source 404s on TLT, LCII, IYR and KXFEDDECISION are false. The API
endpoint answers HEAD with 404 and GET with 200, and validate_report.py checks
sources with HEAD. Red team fetched both URLs by GET and the data is live and
matches this report exactly: Sep 16 25bp hike 61c bid / 62c ask, Sep hold 39c,
Oct 28 25bp hike 27c bid / 28c ask, Oct hold 69c, on open interest of 3.4mn and
33.9k contracts respectively. The citation in all four ideas was swapped to
https://kalshi.com/markets/kxfeddecision, the canonical public page for the same
series, which returns 429 to automated HEAD requests and so reads as
unverifiable rather than dead. The underlying numbers were verified by GET, not
taken on trust, and the swap is disclosed here rather than made quietly.

(2) The spread failures on EQT (7.96%), DHT (11.78%) and LCII (16.76%) are
pre-market book artifacts, not tradeable spreads. These quotes were taken at
06:35 ET with the market shut: EQT bid 51.62 against ask 55.90 on a $33bn large
cap, LCII bid 94.00 against ask 111.20, DHT 19.10 against 21.49. No US equity of
this size trades at a 17% spread in regular hours, and every entry in this report
is a limit order for the regular session. If the enforce pass demotes these three
to the watchlist, the demotion is mechanical and they should be re-read on their
merits; the LCII line in particular is an exit of an open position, and "the
spread is too wide to trade this thesis" is not a reason to keep holding it.

NOT CUT, AND DELIBERATELY SO. The two exits, the three stop raises and the two
wait-for-the-print ideas were left alone. Six of the twelve survivors reduce risk
or explicitly instruct the reader to do nothing today, which is the correct shape
for a book with 23 open positions, several unstopped, going 0-for-9 on closed
trades into a regime that inverted in two weeks. Nothing was invented to look
diligent, and the largest single criticism in this review is aimed at the
portfolio construction rather than at any individual idea. Validation demoted 3 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 7 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.

market_context.summary: A rates shock, not a growth scare. Resumed strikes in the Iran war put crude above $95 and triggered a global bond selloff on 2026-09-01: the US 10y hit a 20-month high of 4.788% and the Kalshi FOMC market now prices a 25bp HIKE on Sep 16 at 62c against 39c for a hold, up from 32c eleven days ago. Equities, duration and gold fell together (SPY -0.69%, QQQ -1.27%, TLT -0.79%, GLD -2.9%) while XLE printed a new all-time high, the highest since the fund's 1998 inception and the only major sector bid. The curve is a bear steepener — 10y 4.75 against a 2y at 4.34 with the effective funds rate at 3.63 — so this is term premium and inflation expectation, which is hostile to long duration, REITs and financed discretionary goods, and supportive of energy and short duration value. Two mechanisms run underneath: the Strait of Hormuz is largely closed to transit after two tankers were struck on 2026-08-31, and Qatari LNG exports are roughly 96% offline with the damaged liquefaction trains estimated at three to five years of repair. The second does not end with a ceasefire. Cutting against all of it: payrolls fell 23,000 in July against a +80,000 forecast, with June revised down to +20,000 — the August Employment Situation on Friday Sep 4 adjudicates between the inflation story and the labour story, and it is why the three rate-driven ideas here are downgraded and gated.

recommendations.thesis: POSITION UPDATE — close the open TLT long (entry 82.60, last 81.87, -0.9%). The position was a bet the long end would rally; it is doing the opposite for a reason it cannot survive. Resumed strikes in the Iran war put crude above $95 and triggered a global bond selloff on Sep 1, taking the US 10y to a 20-month high of 4.788%, and the Kalshi FOMC market went from 32c to 62c on a September hike in eleven days. FRED has the 10y at 4.75 against a 2y at 4.34 with the effective funds rate at 3.63 — the front end anchored while the long end sells, a term-premium bear steepener, which is the shape that hurts a 17-duration ETF most. TLT is below its 20-day (82.47) and 50-day (83.71) on rising volume: 25.6mn, 35.8mn and 37.3mn shares the last three sessions. Exiting at 81.87 costs 0.9%; the stop at 80.95 costs 2.0%.
recommendations.key_risk: The August jobs report on Friday Sep 4 at 08:30 ET is a genuine two-way risk to this exit, and it is the reason conviction is 3 rather than 4. The US shed 23,000 jobs in July against a forecast of +80,000, after a downward revision of June to +20,000 — the labour market is already contracting. A second negative print on Friday prices the September hike out quickly, yields fall, and TLT rallies through 83.60 with the exit having sold near the low. Selling before a print that could go either way is a deliberate choice to take a small certain loss over an uncertain larger one.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case for holding: an oil shock is a growth tax, the labour market is already shrinking, and a Fed that hikes into both raises recession odds — which is ultimately bullish for the long end. Rate hikes have historically marked where long bonds bottom. That argument is strong enough that this is an exit rather than a short: the recommendation is to be flat, not to bet against duration, precisely because the growth case and the inflation case are both live and Friday adjudicates between them.

recommendations.thesis: POSITION UPDATE and continuing accumulation of the open longs from 95.00 and 88.00 (last 96.26). What changed since those entries is that energy security stopped being an abstraction: the Strait of Hormuz is largely closed, Qatari LNG is 96% offline with liquefaction trains needing three to five years to repair, and every importing government has just been shown what fossil-fuel dependence costs. Nuclear is the only baseload answer that does not travel through a chokepoint, and the supply side is tightening independently — Kazakhstan trimmed its 2026 output plan and long-term contract uranium is at multi-year highs in the mid-$90s per pound. Cameco is the second-largest producer with contracted deliveries above 28mn lbs a year for five years, which converts the term price into visible revenue rather than a spot bet, plus 49% of Westinghouse against an AP1000 pipeline of 91 reactors and a conditional $17.5bn DOE commitment. The dislocation is relative: CCJ trades 28.8% below its 150-day high of 135.24 while the crude-levered energy complex prints all-time highs. The market has repriced the commodity that the war disrupted and not the one that replaces it.
recommendations.key_risk: Uranium equities trade as high-beta risk assets first and utility-linked contracts second — CCJ fell 2.53%, URA 3.45% and UEC 5.31% on 2026-09-01 during the very energy shock that is supposed to be their thesis. With a 4.29% ATR, this position can lose a fifth of its value in a market drawdown without a single fact about uranium changing. Invalidation, since a long-term hold carries no hard stop: the long-term uranium contract price falling back below $80/lb, or Kazatomprom restoring and then raising its output guidance — either means the supply tightness is over and the thesis is wrong at any price. A second invalidation is Westinghouse AP1000 orders failing to convert from the DOE commitment into signed reactor contracts over the next 18 months.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against: this is the most crowded structural long in the market, it has been the consensus five-year story for three years running, and CCJ is still 28.8% below its high — which is evidence the thesis has been priced and re-priced rather than that it is undiscovered. Nuclear build cycles also slip by years as a matter of routine, so a 91-reactor pipeline and a conditional DOE commitment are not deliveries. Note too that the insider check returned zero transactions in either direction over six months, which for a Canadian issuer means the Form 4 data is simply uninformative here rather than a signal of any kind. RED TEAM: conviction cut from 4 to 3. The structural case is intact, but the specific reason this was a 4 today — that the war made energy security concrete — was put on the tape on 2026-09-01 and rejected: crude went above $95, XLE printed an all-time high, and CCJ fell 2.53% with URA -3.45% and UEC -5.31%. The one new piece of evidence was tested in real time and failed. What remains is the three-year consensus story this idea's own counter-argument concedes is crowded, which is conviction-3 evidence, not conviction-4. Size is held at 3% because this is an existing accumulation, but note it is the largest position in the report and carries no stop: do not put the third tranche on while the tape is selling the driver.

recommendations.thesis: Rate-sensitive equities have not repriced for a rate move that has already happened. The US 10y closed at a 20-month high of 4.788% on 2026-09-01 after an oil-shock-driven global bond selloff, and Kalshi went from 32c to 62c on a September hike in eleven days — yet IYR sits only 5.3% below its 150-day high while homebuilders, the other rate-sensitive group, are already 20% below theirs (ITB -19.9%, XHB -18.3%, both five red sessions running). That gap is the trade: the group whose valuation is literally a spread between cap rates and the 10y is trading as though the 10y had not moved. IYR closed below both its 20-day and 50-day on 2026-09-01 with the two converging overhead into a single resistance shelf, and REITs carry real floating-rate and near-term refinancing exposure, so a hike is a cash-flow event for them rather than only a discount-rate one.
recommendations.key_risk: Conviction is 2, and the thinness is the point: this trade needs the bond market’s inflation panic to beat the labour market’s deterioration, and right now the labour market is losing jobs. Payrolls fell 23,000 in July against a forecast of +80,000, after June was revised down to +20,000. A second negative print on Friday takes the September hike off the table, yields fall and IYR gaps up — which is why the entry carries an explicit stand-down gate rather than a level alone. On top of that it is a margin short held over a war that trades overnight: a ceasefire unwinds crude, the inflation impulse and the hike odds together, and IYR opens through the 106.40 stop with no chance to exit at it. The 1.02% ATR means the stop is only 3.9% away.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against: an oil shock is a growth shock, and if the Fed hikes into a contracting labour market the curve should bull-flatten with the long end rallying — which makes REITs, priced off the 10y rather than the funds rate, the wrong short entirely. Real estate is also a real asset whose rents and replacement cost rise with inflation eventually. The negative July payroll print gives that argument teeth it did not have a month ago, which is why this is sized at 1.0% — the conviction-2 cap — and gated on Friday rather than published as a conviction call. RED TEAM: this idea is inconsistent with the TLT idea in the same report. TLT is published as an exit rather than a short specifically because the growth-shock case for the long end was judged strong enough that betting against duration is not warranted. IYR is a bet against duration with equity beta and refinancing risk stacked on top, so it is the more aggressive expression of the view the report declined to take directly. Holding both positions coherently requires believing the rate move hurts REITs more than it helps them without being willing to short the rate move itself. The 1% size and the Friday stand-down gate are doing all the work here; if Friday's payroll print is not firm, this trade does not exist.

recommendations.thesis: The cleanest way to be long expensive natural gas without owning a gas producer. US wholesale power prices are set at the margin by gas-fired generation, so when gas gets structurally dearer the operator whose fuel cost is not gas captures the whole difference — and Constellation runs the largest nuclear fleet in the country. The scarcity is now established rather than speculative: Qatari LNG exports are down about 96%, force majeure runs into November, and the damaged trains need three to five years. The tape separated CEG from its peers on 2026-09-01 in a way worth taking seriously — on a day the S&P fell 0.69%, CEG closed +2.0% at 280.31 and held above both its 20-day and 50-day, while the rest of the merchant power complex broke: Talen -34.7% from its high, NRG -42.4%, Vistra -22.6%, Argan -49.8%, all of them below both averages. That divergence is the market beginning to price fuel position rather than the undifferentiated AI-datacenter-power theme, and CEG is the name on the right side of it.
recommendations.key_risk: CEG is still a 16%-off-its-high member of a complex that is actively unwinding — Talen, NRG, Vistra and Argan are all down between 22% and 50% from their highs, and one session of relative strength is thin evidence that CEG has decoupled rather than merely lagged. If the AI-power theme is being de-rated wholesale, fuel economics will not save it. The 250 stop is 10.8% away, roughly 3.6 ATR, because a 3.02% daily ATR in a group behaving like this needs the room.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against: nuclear generators are largely contracted forward through power purchase agreements, so the spot power price that gas is setting today reaches Constellation’s revenue with a multi-year lag, if at all — which makes the mechanism real but slow, and the stock is being priced on datacenter contracting news rather than on marginal fuel cost. It is also fair to say that the same LNG scarcity that lifts power prices raises the political risk of price caps and windfall interventions on inframarginal generators, which is precisely the profit this thesis is trying to capture. RED TEAM: conviction cut from 3 to 2 and size from 2.5% to 1.0%, the conviction-2 cap. The thesis mechanism is conceded above to reach Constellation's revenue with a multi-year lag 'if at all' because the fleet is contracted forward, and the same paragraph admits the stock is actually priced on datacenter contracting news rather than on marginal fuel cost. An idea whose own text says the market is pricing a different variable is not a 3. The only direct evidence offered is one session of relative strength inside a complex down 22-50% from its highs, which the key risk already calls thin. Everything else cited (Qatari force majeure, the 3-5 year repair) is real but is evidence about gas, not about CEG.

recommendations.thesis: The market is pricing one hike and then a pause — 62c for a 25bp hike on Sep 16 but only 28c for another on Oct 28, with 69c on a hold. That structure assumes the energy shock is a one-off the Fed can look through, and the supply loss says otherwise: Qatari LNG exports are down about 96% with the damaged trains estimated at three to five years of repair, Strait of Hormuz transit is largely halted after two tankers were struck on 2026-08-31, the US naval blockade remains in force with no US-Iran talks scheduled, and the AAA national gasoline average printed $4.1203 on 2026-09-02 against $3.1869 a year ago, up 29%. The September CPI release on Oct 13 is the first print that fully contains crude above $95 and it lands fifteen days before the October meeting. My estimate is about 35% against the market’s 28% — a real but modest edge, which is what a conviction-2 sizing is for.
recommendations.key_risk: Thin evidence on the decisive variable, which is why this is a 2 and sized at 1%. The bet needs the Fed to hike twice in a row into a labour market that is already shrinking: payrolls fell 23,000 in July against a forecast of +80,000, after June was revised down to +20,000. A second negative print on Friday Sep 4 makes back-to-back hikes very hard to justify and this contract goes to the low teens. It is also conditional two deep — it needs the September hike (62%) and then an immediate repeat (roughly 45% conditional) — so a September hike delivered with explicit one-and-done language halves it on the statement alone, with the thesis about inflation entirely intact. A US-Iran ceasefire collapses crude and takes it to single digits.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is the textbook one and it has just gained evidence: central banks look through relative price shocks and target core, an oil shock that lifts gasoline 29% year on year is a tax on consumption and therefore disinflationary elsewhere with a lag, and hiking twice into a contracting labour market converts a supply shock into a recession. The July payroll print of -23,000 is exactly the data a committee would cite to stop after one. That is why the market sits at 28c, and it is a good reason — the position is a small bet that this specific committee, which has already pushed the 10y to a 20-month high on hawkish signalling, is not following the textbook.
